claim: The B140 dangle fix requires both `TrimGated`, which limits journal trimming to the committed fold cursor, and `CursorInSnap`, which atomically commits the fold cursor with the snap edges.
If `TrimGated` is enabled without `CursorInSnap`, separate `GCommitEdges` and `GCommitCursor` steps can publish the durable cursor ahead of the edges it claims to cover, allowing a dangle.
If `CursorInSnap` is enabled without `TrimGated`, a leader can trim past what any committed snap covers because the trim bound still consults an in-memory fold cursor.
The merged `m_merged` configuration was green with `TrimGated = TRUE` and `CursorInSnap = TRUE`, while `m_both_buggy`, `m_cursorskip`, and `m_trimonly` violated `INV_NO_LOSS` under the same bounds.
The B140 dangle model battery is reproduced with `docs/superpowers/models/run_b140danglemerge.sh`.

The physical GC destructive gate is open only when the universe is authoritative, the frontier namespace count is nonzero, the proven frontier equals the namespace universe, and neither anomalies nor carried holds suppress destruction.
Equality of an empty `CatalogUniverse` and empty `FrontierProven` is not sufficient destructive authority; an empty universe keeps physical condemnation and deletion suppressed.

Catalog-only pre-fold erasure of a proved `Removing` lifecycle row is independent of the later physical destructive gate and must not be suppressed by unrelated later-round anomalies or carried holds.

`Gc::runRegularRound` invokes `Gc::drainCompletedRemoving` immediately after lease acquisition and before heartbeat work, DEFER, the hot stream LIST, the authoritative catalog cut, plan construction, or fold.
`CatalogLifecycleReconciler::selectEligible` accepts only an exact catalog row in `Removing` whose same-life row in the authoritative adopted parent has cleanup evidence and no durable hold.

The completed-removing drain uses `CasRefCatalog::deleteCompletedRemovingAtSnapshot` for an exact catalog CAS, resolves its outcome, and rescans until no eligible row remains; it performs no physical cleanup.

The `CaGcDestructiveGateCore` model does not cover the non-authoritative-universe posture, where production must suppress destruction regardless of the other physical-gate conjuncts; that posture is asserted by `CasGcFrontierGate.HiddenPlusOneInAnUnknownNamespaceIsRefusedByTheProductionDefault`.
The B160 GC lease fix adds an advisory heartbeat register `hb`; a follower steals only when both `(owner, seq)` and `hb` remain frozen throughout its observation window.
Without the heartbeat register, a slow-but-alive incumbent whose `seq` changes only once per round can appear frozen across a follower window and be falsely deposed.
The heartbeat is not safety-critical for lease fencing: `NoEpochCollision` remains green with `EnableHeartbeat = FALSE`, while the heartbeat is load-bearing for `NoFalseSteal`.
A DEFER invocation may inspect one bounded namespace-janitor page under suppression, but it must retain a valid cursor so the next authorized fold retries that page.
Advancing the janitor cursor from page `A` to `B` during a suppressed DEFER can form the fair `A-defer -> B-fold -> A` cycle, permanently skipping page `A` and violating `EventuallyDeadAReclaimed`.
The root-local part-manifest design retired the `listedTok` token-diff discovery skip: a LIST match may not authorize skipping a manifest or owner-transition fold read.

`supportsListTokens()` and `tokenForList` expose a LIST-derived incarnation token only for the blob-condemn exact-delete-versus-`HEAD` decision, never for skipping a manifest or owner-transition fold read.
The ref-log intake walk still issues the exact-key `GET` at `cursor + 1` even when `cursor == tail`; an absent expected-next key with no higher witness is the proof that sets `frontier_proven`.

The four `EnableTokenDiff = TRUE` configurations `stage5_tokendiff`, `sab_skipchangedshard`, `sab_skipparksdeadprecommit`, and `fix_skipparksdeadprecommit` were retired because no production seam legitimately consumes a LIST-derived token as authority to skip the fold read.

The `stage5_lazytrim` positive safety claim under `EnableLazyTrim = TRUE` remains unproven by TLC after a four-hour `-workers 1` run, with `1,333,723,653` states generated, `233,198,128` distinct, and `24,395,446` queued.

The sharding arm remains unproven because `sab_crosssharddisplacement`, `sab_reducerownsfence`, and `stage5_sharding` all hit the model error `UnchangedCompositeVars`; consequently `EnableSharding`'s cross-shard displacement and reducer-owns-fence guards were not exercised by TLC.
The root-local part-manifest model assumes backend LIST consistency for shard discovery; the implementation must confirm strongly consistent LIST semantics per backend.
The GC round DEFER mechanism bounds consecutive deferrals with `MaxDefer`; once the bound is reached, `GBegin` and weak fairness drive `GFold` so `unfolded` eventually returns to `{}`.
Removing the `deferCount < MaxDefer` guard permits a fair infinite DEFER sequence in which nonempty `unfolded` deltas are never folded, violating `EventuallyFolded`.
Graduating a blob without first checking that `unfolded` contains no pending delta for that blob can physically delete it after a protective `+1` lands after the fold cut, violating `NoOverDelete`.
The delete guard in `GComplete` must force a fold for any pending delta touching the candidate blob, and `unfolded` carries both `add` and `del` signs.
`Indeg` is read from the sealed `folded` snapshot only; a delta added after the fold cut remains in `unfolded` and is protected by the pending-delta guard rather than by the in-degree check.

FOLD and DEFER are mutually exclusive in an idle round: `DeferRound` is enabled only when `~GraduationDue` and its deferral condition hold, while `GBegin` is enabled for graduation or an exhausted honest defer budget.

The pinned TLC runner had to recognize both `Temporal properties were violated.` and the named-property form `Temporal property EventuallyFolded was violated.`; otherwise `sab_unbounded_defer` was misclassified as an error.
Removing the namespace registry requires two independent coordinates: a never-reused per-`(ns,shard)` incarnation for identity and the pool-global GC round as the newborn shard's self-fence.
A newborn shard is fenced to the current `gcRound` at birth, and GC discovers and fences every present shard by LIST each round.
The namespace registry can be deleted without an ephemeral `pending-newborns` fallback because the newborn self-floor plus per-round LIST fencing preserves `INV_NO_DANGLING`.

Neither the pool-global round nor the incarnation alone is sufficient: dropping the newborn self-floor violates `INV_NO_DANGLING`, while dropping incarnation from the fold cursor permits an ABA dangle.
Shard reclaim must wait until the shard journal is fully folded, including its tombstone, before token-guarded `deleteExact`; deleting earlier can orphan a folded edge and leak the target blob.
Incarnation monotonicity is required per `(ns,shard)`, not globally: incarnations may collide across different shards because the cursor key includes `(shard, incarnation)`.
A delete-and-recreate of the same `(ns,shard)` must draw an incarnation strictly greater than that path's high-water mark; reusing an incarnation on the same path causes an ABA error.
The shard-incarnation model assumes discovery equals present shards and therefore assumes strongly consistent backend LIST semantics.

`WipeEpoch` models genuine loss of the durable epoch object independently of sabotage flags and is guarded by `epochWiped` so it fires at most once per behavior; repeated loss is outside this gate's scope.

After a genuine post-wipe condition `epoch = 0 /\ epochCeiling > 0`, `RemintEpoch` may re-mint only when no live unfenced mount for the actor exists, while `RemintEpochDecom` requires a crashed actor and a Drift-aware terminal surviving mount unless `SabDecomBlindBypass` is enabled.
`WipeEpoch` alone can violate `WriterEpochMonotoneUnique`: after a write at epoch 1, wiping the durable epoch to 0 leaves `wrote` containing `(A,1)` while the live epoch is 0.

The honest `RemintEpoch` branch's hardcoded epoch value `1` can collide with a historical `(A,1)` already in `fencedEpochs`, allowing a live unfenced mount under a previously fenced pair and violating `FenceCostsEpoch`.
Replacing the honest `RemintEpoch` literal `1` with `epochCeiling + 1` is an unimplemented candidate refinement that would avoid historical fenced-epoch collisions.

The mount model's honest `RemintEpoch` path over-approximates production because it omits the code precondition `serverRootSubtreeEmpty`; the model's honest `FenceCostsEpoch` counterexample is therefore conservative rather than proof that production reaches the same state.

The v9 recovery and wedge paths must recheck the captured mount-fence generation immediately before every mutation: `slot-occupy`, `_ckpt` publication, install, unwedge, or equivalent retry publication.

The recovery-generation model identifies an operation by `<< actor, generation, op >>`; using only `<< actor, generation >>` aliases distinct same-generation operations and can hide an ack for bytes that were never written.

`AckedOpsAreDurable` requires every acknowledged operation identity to be in `durable`; with byte comparison disabled, `WedgeRetryOccupied` can falsely acknowledge a second same-generation operation from the first operation's bytes.
Once a successor's `SealSlot` occupies the key, `WedgeRetryOccupied` must reject the retry regardless of the presented generation; the seal is conclusive during the pre-seal race.
The `MaxAdmissions` bound limits how many operations or recoveries a behavior admits for TLC state-space feasibility; it is a search bound, not a safety claim.

The production strict ordering allocates the durable writer epoch before claiming the mount, as documented at `CasStore.cpp:312-316`; the model constraint is `StrictOrderMount == mount = None /\ mount.epoch > 0`.

The `CaCasMountCore` recovery-generation gate does not model the `_ckpt` CAS itself or prove that `slot-occupy`, `_ckpt`, and install present the same rechecked generation; that remains a plan obligation.
The catalog-token half of zombie-install prevention remains owned by `CaRefCatalogCore`; the mount model proves only the generation credential and the install must present both credentials.

The CAS worklog's observed S42 stale-edge defect occurs when a precommit's `+1` edges fold into in-degree, allocation then aborts, and the orphan-manifest sweep deletes the now-unowned manifest without decrementing those folded edges.

The orphan-manifest sweep's premise that an unowned manifest has no folded edges is false after a precommit `+1` folds, leaving stranded in-degree edges with no possible `-1` after the manifest is deleted.

Across 959 decoded ref-log transactions, the worklog measured 7,565 manifest edges over 4,573 distinct manifests; 2,991 manifests carried both an add and a remove edge, so 39.6% of intake manifest fetches were cross-transaction re-reads.

The measured manifest-read redundancy is cross-transaction rather than intra-transaction: a round-scoped manifest-body cache could avoid it, while an operation- or transaction-scoped cache would save nothing.

The GC duration study found round time dominated by serial object-store request latency: a 30-minute round represented about 3.42 million serial round trips at approximately 0.5 ms each, with repeated manifest work secondary.

The worklog observed incomplete LIST answers for the same ref-log prefix: `0x1430c` and `0x1430d` were present by `HEAD` but omitted from a fold scan after `0x1430e`, and deletion, append ordering, and not-yet-landed writes were excluded for that occurrence.
When probe A detects a ref-scan disagreement, the fold must abort without advancing the cursor or deleting anything; the live detector stopped all seven observed folds this way.
In fsck terminology, `dangling` means referenced-but-missing, while the CAS soak's stuck class was `unreachable` or `awaiting-gc`; `dangling` was zero in every recorded run.

The ref-lane implementation replaced nested apply-marker and durable-floor encodings with `RefLaneState{Ready,Writing,Wedged,NeedsRecovery,Closed,Faulted}`; confirmation is `Ready`-only and terminal `Closed`/`Faulted` states are non-retriable.
A Created-then-moved-fence recovery hole transfers exact known durability to `NeedsRecovery` instead of losing the durable transaction.

Treating a vanished catalog as an empty catalog is unsafe: the retry path could replace every namespace's catalog with a single mutation's output via create-if-absent; `PoolMeta::admitOrValidate` is the fail-closed analogue.
A destructive gate based only on `proven == total` accepts an empty universe because `0 == 0`; the gate therefore needs an explicit nonempty-authority predicate.
